objective: Generalize core idea discovery, selection and explanation across different positional move types, preserving purpose, reply contrast, delayed realization and price.

heldout_cases.game: Daniel V. Pedersen - Jacob Aagaard, Denmark 2012
heldout_cases.criterion: Explain the useful route toward d2/b3/c5 if supported by returned play; distinguish transient defense from redeployment. Preserve opponent central play and costs; do not import the book continuation.

heldout_cases.kind: exchange to change the remaining pieces and pawn play
heldout_cases.criterion: Explain removal of the original knight/bishop and how remaining pieces and e5/d4 access differ if observed. Do not describe equal material alone or infer a permanent weak/strong square from its name.

heldout_cases.kind: bishop exchange and removal of a defender
heldout_cases.criterion: Explain bishop exchange or interruption of the c5 defender and observed remaining-piece use if supported; preserve actual reference purpose and response costs without importing the book line.
heldout_cases.reason: Both original heldouts exposed failures and became development cases. Add exactly one fourth screen position to retain an independent check after the common exchange fix; do not discard either earlier failure.

heldout_protocol: No engine output or product commentary for these two positions before a common implementation is frozen. First failure remains a failure if subsequently used for changes. Book purpose is a question, not a forced reference or evaluation truth.

constraints.actual_screen_cases: Four distinct positions total: Ng8, Nb1, Nxd4, then one new Be7 after the first heldouts failed. No additional positions.
constraints.validation: Reuse exact owned prior root reports and targeted semantic boundaries; no broad suite or long performance sampling

initial_common_hypotheses: Any legal MoveIntent candidate currently disables MovePurpose discovery even if unsupported; a speculative attack can hide an observed route/support/exchange question.
MovePurpose uses static type order and the first candidate instead of considering an observed functional use across candidates.
Prepared intent admission is limited to non-capturing first actions on the played root; existing functional readers and two-root purpose composition must be reused, not reimplemented for each motif.

source.title: Aagaard, Grandmaster Preparation: Positional Play
source.lesson: A concrete relation can be true without being the important idea. Useful piece improvement, relevant weakness and opponent resources must be connected; exchange changes which apparent weaknesses can actually be used.

findings: First functional contact and first legal destination can displace a later witnessed useful role; selection and composition used different paths.
Root-PV-only discovery discards useful routes present in owned reply surveys. An independent full-reply survey is now allowed to refine the purpose without reusing a forced plan test.
Twenty-second functional response work was rejected by a frontend limit branch that only admitted the old short work shape.
A functional reply added to a selected comparison did not carry its search ownership; the frontend discarded the composed body.
Protection discovery ignored a newly supplied guard against the actually observed first reply.
A route returning to the original square cannot causally assign a later plan to the initial move.
